rationale: No supported optimization can be applied safely while preserving build/test coverage. P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT has measured CI evidence (experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508, experiment:batch-interactive-three--112e2b2e7fbe04b8) showing elapsed savings from adding job timeouts, but its precondition requires representative successful-duration history; this repository has only a single CI run with no recorded duration, and every job installs dependencies from source each run (brew install luajit --HEAD on macOS; git clone + make + sudo make install of LuaJIT on Linux), so cold runs are unbound and a fixed timeout risks failing valid slow builds (contraindication: valid slow runs exceed the proposed limit). P-LIT-GHA-CACHE (cache dependency downloads) is contraindicated because the fetched dependencies are unpinned/mutable (luajit --HEAD, LuaJIT master) with no lockfile, and the pattern warns against caching mutable/untrusted content; pinning dependencies would be an unrelated behavior change. P-LIT-FAIL-FAST and the Bazel patterns do not fit (no matrix, no Bazel). P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE could cancel superseded runs, but required-checks safety is unverified (required_checks status is not_verified), and the pattern itself flags that branch-protection/required-check review is needed separately. Since no candidate satisfies its preconditions without risking coverage, the workflow is unchanged.
